title: Theory of associating polymers with annealed and quenched sticker disorder: Mean-field solution and phase behavior
authors: Sofia Moschin, Achille Giacometti, Amos Maritan, Angelo Rosa
abstract: We develop a density-functional theory for solutions of associating polymers where attractions among charged monomers (stickers) are represented by local binary degrees of freedom, which are randomly placed along the chains. Extending the original Garel and Orland's field-theoretic scheme for single-chain systems to an ensemble of interacting chains, we give the exact formulations of the model in both cases of annealed and quenched distributions of charges which we solve at the mean-field level. The solution produces qualitatively different free energy functionals. In the annealed case, the theory naturally yields a nontrivial scalar order parameter for the fraction of bonded sticker monomers and a self-consistent mass-action law at the saddle point. By contrast, in the quenched case no independent bonding order parameter emerges and the main effect is a renormalization of the effective two-body and three-body interaction parameters. The formulation is microscopic at the Hamiltonian level and, within the same field-theoretic framework, provides a systematic starting point for fluctuation corrections beyond the mean-field approximation.
summary: This paper develops a mean-field density-functional theory for associating polymers with sticker interactions under both mobile (annealed) and frozen (quenched) disorder. It rigorously shows that the statistical treatment of disorder leads to qualitatively different thermodynamic predictions, particularly regarding the emergence of an order parameter. This work advances the understanding of complex self-assembly processes relevant to biomolecular condensates.
main_problem: The study develops a density-functional theory to determine the phase behavior of associating polymers when the sticker interactions are subject to either annealed (mobile) or quenched (fixed) disorder.
main_result: The theory yields distinct results for the two disorder types: the annealed case supports an independent bonding order parameter, while the quenched case primarily causes renormalization of interaction parameters. Both approaches provide a systematic starting point for fluctuation corrections.
method: The authors employ field-theoretic methods, extending existing schemes to formulate the model at the mean-field level using saddle point approximations for both annealed (ensemble averaging) and quenched (replica trick) disorder treatments.
model_or_system: The system consists of polymer chains with monomers possessing binary 'stickers' that mediate reversible attractions. The Hamiltonian includes terms for chain connectivity, volume interactions ($w_2, w_3$), and sticker-sticker interactions ($\propto w_{	ext{stick}}^2, w_{	ext{stick}}^3$).
key_observables: Free energy density ($ eta F/V$), scalar order parameter (for the annealed case), and renormalized effective interaction parameters.

main_assumptions: The primary approximations are the mean-field solution via saddle point methods, and for the quenched case, the use of the replica trick. The theory is microscopic but provides a starting point beyond these approximations.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the Hamiltonian and reformulating it using density fields. It then derives separate mean-field solutions for the annealed (ensemble average) and quenched (replica trick) cases, comparing their resulting free energy functionals and phase behavior.
why_interesting: While focused on polymer physics, the rigorous comparison between annealed and quenched disorder statistics in a complex many-body system is highly relevant to understanding glassy dynamics or disordered quantum materials where local environments are fluctuating versus fixed.
